Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 20, verses 1–8:

Explanation of the words:

Ta-Ha (طه): i.e., "O man."

Illa tadhkiratan (إلا تذكرة): i.e., only so that whoever fears the punishment of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, may be reminded by the Qur'an.

ʿAla al-ʿArshi istawa (على العرش استوى): i.e., He rose above it and exalted Himself over it.

Wa ma taht al-thara (وما تحت الثرى): al-thara is the moist soil; he means what lies beneath the seven earths.

Akhfa (وأخفى): i.e., more hidden than the secret, which is what Allah knows and has decreed to exist, and which will occur, but has not yet occurred.

Al-husna (الحسنى): the feminine of al-ahsan, the superlative of al-hasan (good).

Meaning of the verses:

Allah the Exalted says, ﴿Ta-Ha﴾. The word Ta-Ha may be one of the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'ah), and it may also mean "O man." Ibn Jarir preferred the latter view, since Ta-Ha with the meaning "O man" is attested in the Arabic language. On this understanding, the meaning of the speech is "O man, We did not send down the Qur'an upon you so that you would be distressed," in answer to al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, who said that Muhammad was made miserable by this Qur'an that was revealed to him because of its obligations. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, negated that and said: ﴿We did not send down the Qur'an upon you to make you wretched, but only as a reminder for whoever fears [Allah]﴾. Rather, We sent it down to be a reminder through which whoever fears his Lord is reminded, so that he turns to His obedience, bearing in that cause whatever harm he may encounter from his polytheist people who associate others with Allah, disbelieve in His Book, and deny His Messenger. And His saying: ﴿A revelation from He who created the earth and the high heavens﴾ means: this Qur'an, which We did not send down for you to be distressed by it, but as a reminder for whoever fears, has been sent down as a revelation from Allah, who created the earth and the high heavens. ﴿The Most Merciful, who is established upon the Throne﴾ means: the Merciful of this world and the Hereafter and their Compassionate, who rose above His Throne in a manner befitting Him, governing His creatures. To Him belongs ﴿whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth and whatever is between them and whatever is beneath the soil﴾, meaning the seven earths. As for His saying ﴿And if you speak aloud﴾, O Messenger, or ﴿keep it secret﴾, ﴿then indeed He knows the secret and [what is] more hidden﴾ than the secret, which is what Allah has decreed and which will occur at its appointed time; Allah the Exalted knows it, while a human being does not yet know it. And His saying: ﴿Allah – there is no deity except Him﴾, meaning Allah, the one truly worthy of worship, and there is no one truly worthy of worship besides Him. ﴿To Him belong the most beautiful names﴾, which belong to none but Him and cannot belong to any other of His creatures. In this way the Exalted made Himself known to His servants so that they would know Him, fear Him, and love Him, believe in Him and obey Him, and thereby attain perfection and happiness. So all praise is due to Allah, and His is the favor.

Guidance from the verses:

1. Refutation of the view that the legal obligations of the Shariah are burdensome and oppressive to the servant.

2. Affirmation of the doctrine of revelation and the proof of Muhammad's prophethood.

3. Affirmation of Allah's attributes, such as istiwa', and the obligation to believe in them without ta'wil (figurative reinterpretation), ta'til (denial), or tashbih (likening), but affirming them in the manner befitting their Owner, the Mighty and Majestic.

4. Affirmation of Allah's lordship over everything.

5. Affirmation of Tawhid and the establishment of Allah's beautiful names and exalted attributes.

Rather, We sent it down to be a reminder through which whoever fears his Lord is reminded, so that he turns to His obedience, bearing in that cause whatever harm he may encounter from his polytheist people who associate others with Allah, disbelieve in His Book, and deny His Messenger. And His saying: ﴿A revelation from He who created the earth and the high heavens﴾ means: this Qur'an, which We did not send down for you to be distressed by it, but as a reminder for whoever fears, has been sent down as a revelation from Allah, who created the earth and the high heavens. ﴿The Most Merciful, who is established upon the Throne﴾ means: the Merciful of this world and the Hereafter and their Compassionate, who rose above His Throne in a manner befitting Him, governing His creatures. To Him belongs ﴿whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth and whatever is between them and whatever is beneath the soil﴾, meaning the seven earths. As for His saying ﴿And if you speak aloud﴾, O Messenger, or ﴿keep it secret﴾, ﴿then indeed He knows the secret and [what is] more hidden﴾ than the secret, which is what Allah has decreed and which will occur at its appointed time; Allah the Exalted knows it, while a human being does not yet know it. And His saying: ﴿Allah – there is no deity except Him﴾, meaning Allah, the one truly worthy of worship, and there is no one truly worthy of worship besides Him. ﴿To Him belong the most beautiful names﴾, which belong to none but Him and cannot belong to any other of His creatures. Guidance from the verses:

1. Refutation of the view that the legal obligations of the Shariah are burdensome and oppressive to the servant.

2. Affirmation of the doctrine of revelation and the proof of Muhammad's prophethood.

3. Affirmation of Allah's attributes, such as istiwa', and the obligation to believe in them without ta'wil (figurative reinterpretation), ta'til (denial), or tashbih (likening), but affirming them in the manner befitting their Owner, the Mighty and Majestic.

4. Affirmation of Allah's lordship over everything.

5. Affirmation of Tawhid and the establishment of Allah's beautiful names and exalted attributes.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 20, verses 17–24:**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Wa ma tilka biyaminika ya Musa* (And what is that in your right hand, O Musa): The interrogative is for confirmation (istiqrar), so that the miracle may be built upon it, namely its transformation into a live serpent.

*Atawakka'u alayha* (I lean upon it): i.e., I rely on it.

*Wa ahushshu biha ala ghanami* (And I beat down with it upon my sheep): I strike with it the leaves of the trees so that they fall and the sheep eat them.

*Wa li fiha ma'aribu ukhra* (And I have other uses for it): i.e., other needs, such as carrying provisions by hanging them on it and then bearing them on the shoulder, and killing vermin.

*Hayyatun tas'a* (A serpent that moves): i.e., a great serpent, moving on its belly swiftly like the small serpent called the jann.

*Sirataha al-ula* (Its former state): i.e., to its first condition before it had become a serpent.

*Ila janahika* (Into your wing): i.e., into your left side, under the upper arm to the armpit.

*Bayda'a min ghayri su'* (White, without blemish): i.e., without leprosy, shining like a ray of the sun.

*Idhhab ila Fir'awn* (Go to Pharaoh): i.e., as a messenger to him.

*Innahu taghā* (Indeed he has transgressed): he exceeded the limit in disbelief to the point of claiming divinity.

**Meaning of the verses:**

The noble context continues with Musa and his Lord, may He be exalted, when the Lord, who knows him and what is in his hand better than he does, said: "*And what is that in your right hand, O Musa?*" He asks in order to establish that what is in his hand is a staff of dry wood; then when it turns into a moving serpent, he will know that it is a sign which his Lord, the Possessor of overwhelming power, gave him to send him to Pharaoh and his chiefs. Musa answered his Lord, saying: "*It is my staff; I lean upon it and beat down with it upon my sheep*", meaning he strikes the dry trees so that the leaves fall and the sheep eat them, "*and I have other uses for it*", i.e., other needs, such as carrying provisions and water by hanging them on it and placing it on the shoulder as is the custom of shepherds, and perhaps he kills harmful vermin with it, such as scorpions and snakes. Then his Lord, mighty and majestic, said to him: "*Throw it down, O Musa*", so he threw it from his hand, "*and behold, it was a serpent moving swiftly*", i.e., a great serpent moving on its belly like the small serpent called the jann, so Musa was frightened of it and turned to flee. Then the Lord, may He be exalted, said to him: "*Take hold of it and do not fear; We shall return it to its former state*", i.e., We shall return it to a staff as it was before its transformation into a serpent. He indeed took it, and behold, it was his staff that had been in his right hand. Then He commanded him, saying: "*And draw your hand into your wing*", i.e., the right hand into the left side, "*it will come out white, without blemish*", i.e., without leprosy. He did so: he placed it under his upper arm at the armpit, then drew it out, and behold, it was gleaming as if it were a piece of the moon, or as white as snow or even more so. And His saying, "*as another sign*", i.e., a sign for you indicating your prophethood, since the first was the transformation of the staff into a moving serpent as if it were a jann. And His saying: "*that We may show you of Our greater signs*", i.e., We turned the staff into a serpent for you and made your hand come out white in order that We might show you some of the indications of Our power and the greatness of Our dominion. And His saying: "*Go to Pharaoh; indeed he has transgressed*": because of the wonders of His power that He showed him, He commanded him to go to Pharaoh as a messenger to him, commanding him to worship God alone and to send the Children of Israel with him so that he might bring them out to the Holy Land of Syria. His saying "*indeed he has transgressed*" means he exceeded his station and overstepped his bounds as a human being, for he came to claim lordship and divinity, when he said: "*I am your lord, the Most High*" [al-Nazi'at: 24], and said: "*I know of no god for you other than myself*" [al-Qasas: 38]. Then what transgression is greater than this transgression?

**Guidance of the verses:**

From the guidance of these verses:

1. Establishing the prophethood of the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), since reports of this kind are only valid from one to whom revelation is given.

2. The recommendation of taking hold of things that are not repugnant with the right hand.

3. The legitimacy of carrying a staff.

4. The sunnah of prophets tending sheep.

5. The legitimacy of training in weapons before using them in battles.

6. The sign of Musa in the transformation of the staff into a serpent and the emergence of the white hand as if it were snow or the light of the sun.

7. Clarification of transgression: it is a servant claiming what is not his, such as divinity and the like.

*Ila janahika* (Into your wing): i.e., into your left side, under the upper arm to the armpit.

*Bayda'a min ghayri su'* (White, without blemish): i.e., without leprosy, shining like a ray of the sun.

*Idhhab ila Fir'awn* (Go to Pharaoh): i.e., as a messenger to him.

*Innahu taghā* (Indeed he has transgressed): he exceeded the limit in disbelief to the point of claiming divinity.

**Meaning of the verses:**

The noble context continues with Musa and his Lord, may He be exalted, when the Lord, who knows him and what is in his hand better than he does, said: "*And what is that in your right hand, O Musa?*" He asks in order to establish that what is in his hand is a staff of dry wood; then when it turns into a moving serpent, he will know that it is a sign which his Lord, the Possessor of overwhelming power, gave him to send him to Pharaoh and his chiefs. Musa answered his Lord, saying: "*It is my staff; I lean upon it and beat down with it upon my sheep*", meaning he strikes the dry trees so that the leaves fall and the sheep eat them, "*and I have other uses for it*", i.e., other needs, such as carrying provisions and water by hanging them on it and placing it on the shoulder as is the custom of shepherds, and perhaps he kills harmful vermin with it, such as scorpions and snakes. Then his Lord, mighty and majestic, said to him: "*Throw it down, O Musa*", so he threw it from his hand, "*and behold, it was a serpent moving swiftly*", i.e., a great serpent moving on its belly like the small serpent called the jann, so Musa was frightened of it and turned to flee. Then the Lord, may He be exalted, said to him: "*Take hold of it and do not fear; We shall return it to its former state*", i.e., We shall return it to a staff as it was before its transformation into a serpent. He indeed took it, and behold, it was his staff that had been in his right hand. Then He commanded him, saying: "*And draw your hand into your wing*", i.e., the right hand into the left side, "*it will come out white, without blemish*", i.e., without leprosy. He did so: he placed it under his upper arm at the armpit, then drew it out, and behold, it was gleaming as if it were a piece of the moon, or as white as snow or even more so. And His saying, "*as another sign*", i.e., a sign for you indicating your prophethood, since the first was the transformation of the staff into a moving serpent as if it were a jann. And His saying: "*that We may show you of Our greater signs*", i.e., We turned the staff into a serpent for you and made your hand come out white in order that We might show you some of the indications of Our power and the greatness of Our dominion. And His saying: "*Go to Pharaoh; indeed he has transgressed*": because of the wonders of His power that He showed him, He commanded him to go to Pharaoh as a messenger to him, commanding him to worship God alone and to send the Children of Israel with him so that he might bring them out to the Holy Land of Syria. His saying "*indeed he has transgressed*" means he exceeded his station and overstepped his bounds as a human being, for he came to claim lordship and divinity, when he said: "*I am your lord, the Most High*" [al-Nazi'at: 24], and said: "*I know of no god for you other than myself*" [al-Qasas: 38]. Then what transgression is greater than this transgression?

**Guidance of the verses:**

From the guidance of these verses:

1. Establishing the prophethood of the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), since reports of this kind are only valid from one to whom revelation is given.

2. The recommendation of taking hold of things that are not repugnant with the right hand.

3. The legitimacy of carrying a staff.

4. The sunnah of prophets tending sheep.

5. The legitimacy of training in weapons before using them in battles.

6. The sign of Musa in the transformation of the staff into a serpent and the emergence of the white hand as if it were snow or the light of the sun.

7. Clarification of transgression: it is a servant claiming what is not his, such as divinity and the like.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 20, verses 25–35:

Explanation of the words:

"Ashrah li sadri" (Expand my chest for me): i.e., widen it so that I can bear the message.

"Wa yassir li amri" (And ease my task for me): i.e., make it easy so that I am able to carry it out.

"Wahlul ʿuqdatan min lisani" (And untie a knot from my tongue): i.e., a speech impediment, so that those I address may understand me.

"Ashdud bihi azri" (Strengthen my back through him): i.e., strengthen my back by means of him.

"Wa ashrikhu fi amri" (And make him a partner in my task): i.e., make him a prophet, as You have granted me prophethood.

The meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with the account of Musa (peace be upon him) and his Lord, the Exalted. After Allah commanded Musa to go to Pharaoh to call him to worship Allah alone, and to send the Children of Israel with Musa so that he would take them to the land of al-Quds, Musa (peace be upon him) said to his Lord, the Exalted: ﴿Expand my chest for me﴾ so that I may bear the burdens of the message, ﴿and ease my task for me﴾, meaning make my mission easy for me and grant me help in carrying it out, for it is difficult and arduous. ﴿And untie a knot from my tongue﴾: that knot which arose because of the ember that he put into his mouth by the design of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. When Pharaoh intended to kill him, he had placed him on his lap while playing with him, and Musa took hold of Pharaoh's beard and pulled it, so Pharaoh became angry. Asiya said to him that he lacked understanding because of his young age, and she told him to test him by placing jewels on a tray and an ember in a basin, and presenting them to him. If he takes the jewels, then he is intelligent, and you may do with him as you wish; but if he takes the ember, then he lacks understanding, so do not heed him and do not be distressed by his act. The tray and the basin were presented to Musa, and he reached his hand toward the basin by the design of Allah and took an ember, and this became the cause of this knot. So Musa asked his Lord to untie it from his tongue so that he could speak clearly when addressing Pharaoh and make himself clear, and thus be understood, and so fulfil his message. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And untie a knot from my tongue, that they may understand my speech﴾.

And His saying, related about Musa: ﴿And appoint for me a minister from my family, Harun, my brother﴾, meaning he asked Allah to make for him, from his brother Harun, a helper in conveying the message and bearing its burdens. His saying: ﴿Strengthen my back through him﴾, meaning strengthen my back by means of him. His saying: ﴿And make him a partner in my task﴾, which is by making him a prophet and sending him so that Harun would be a prophet and messenger. Musa (peace be upon him) gave as the reason for this request his saying: ﴿So that we may glorify You much, and remember You much﴾, and His saying ﴿Indeed You are ever, of us, All-Seeing﴾, meaning You have been, regarding us, one who sees: nothing of our affair is hidden from You. This is from Musa a means of seeking nearness to Allah for the acceptance of his supplication, and in what he asked of his Lord he sought nearness through His knowledge of him, of his brother, and of their condition.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The obligation of turning to Allah in everything that concerns the servant.

2- The legitimacy of taking precautions and preparing for what the servant intends to undertake.

3- The virtue of glorifying and remembering Allah, and of seeking nearness through the Names and Attributes of Allah.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 20, verses 36–41:

Explanation of the words:

*Qad utīta suʾlaka* (﴿قد أوتيت سؤلك﴾): that is, what you asked for: the expansion of your breast, the facilitating of your affair, the loosening of the knot of your tongue, and the granting of your brother as a messenger.

*Wa-laqad manannā ʿalayka marratan ukhrā* (﴿ولقد مننا عليك مرة أخرى﴾): that is, We bestowed favour upon you another time before this.

*Mā yūḥā* (﴿ما يوحى﴾): that is, concerning your situation, namely His saying: "Cast him..." etc.

*Fī al-tābūt* (﴿في التابوت﴾): that is, the chest.

*Fa-qdhifīhi fī al-yamm* (﴿فاقذفيه في اليم﴾): that is, into the river Nile.

*Wa-li-tuṣnaʿa ʿalā ʿaynī* (﴿ولتصنع على عيني﴾): to be raised under My sight, with My love and My will.

*ʿAlā man yakfuluhu* (﴿على من يكفله﴾): so that he may complete his nursing for him.

*Wa-qatalta nafsan* (﴿وقتلت نفسا﴾): this is the Copt whom you killed in Egypt, which was the house of Pharaoh.

*Fa-najjaynāka mina al-ghamm* (﴿فنجيناك من الغم﴾): when you sought forgiveness from Us, We forgave you, and when they conspired against you to kill you, We delivered you from them.

*Wa-fatannāka futūnan* (﴿وفتناك فتونا﴾): that is, We tested you with a test and afflicted you with a great affliction.

*Jiʾta ʿalā qadar* (﴿جئت على قدر﴾): that is, you came at the appointed time when We willed to send you to Pharaoh.

*Wa-iṣṭanaʿtuka li-nafsī* (﴿واصطنعتك لنفسي﴾): that is, I bestowed upon you those blessings, choosing you to bear Our message.

Meaning of the verses:

The discourse remains in the account of Moses with his Lord, the Exalted. It has already been mentioned that Moses, peace be upon him, asked his Lord for matters to serve as a help to him in bearing his message, and the Exalted answered him with His saying, in this verse [36]: ﴿He said: You have been granted your request, O Moses﴾, that is, what you asked for has been given to you. ﴿And We had already bestowed favour upon you another time﴾, that is, before these requests, when Pharaoh commanded the slaughter of the sons of the Children of Israel, ﴿when We inspired your mother with what was inspired, saying: Cast him into the chest﴾, that is, into the box, ﴿then cast him into the river﴾, that is, the Nile, ﴿and the river will throw him onto the bank, and there will take him an enemy of Mine and an enemy of his﴾. This deliverance is a blessing, and another blessing is contained in His saying: ﴿And I cast upon you love from Me﴾, that is, I bestowed upon you My love, so whoever saw you would love you. Another blessing is: so that you might be raised and nourished under My sight and by My will, I returned you by My arrangement to your mother so that she would nurse you, her eye would be comforted, and she would not grieve over your separation. This is what His saying contains: ﴿When your sister walked and said: Shall I direct you to one who will take charge of him?﴾, that is, for you, for his nursing and rearing. ﴿So We returned you to your mother that her eye might be comforted and she not grieve﴾. Another blessing, and the greatest, is Our deliverance of you from the great distress after you killed a soul and the family of Pharaoh conspired to kill you: ﴿So We delivered you from distress﴾, from killing, and We forgave you the sin of killing. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We tested you with many trials﴾, that is, We afflicted you with a great affliction. Here is its summary in the following points:

1- Your mother's bearing you in the year in which the sons of the Children of Israel were being slain.

2- Your mother casting you into the river.

3- The forbidding of wet-nurses to you until you returned to your mother.

4- Your seizing Pharaoh's beard and his intent to kill you.

5- Your killing of the Copt and the conspiracy of Pharaoh's family to kill you.

6- Your residence in Midian and what you endured of the pains of estrangement.

7- Your losing your way with your family and what befell you of fear and fatigue.

These are some of what falls under His saying: ﴿And We tested you with many trials﴾, and His saying: ﴿Then you stayed for years among the people of Midian﴾, pasturing the sheep of Shuʿayb for ten years, ﴿then you came﴾ from Midian to Mount Sinai ﴿at an appointed time﴾ decreed by Us, a determined promise that you did not know until you met it.

*Wa-iṣṭanaʿtuka li-nafsī*, that is, I created you, reared you, tested you, and brought you at an appointed time I had decreed, to charge you with the burden of the message to Pharaoh and the Children of Israel: to Pharaoh, to call him to worship Us and to send the Children of Israel with you to the land of return; and to the Children of Israel, to guide and reform them and prepare them for happiness and perfection in both abodes, if they believe and remain upright.

Guidance from the verses:

Guidance from the verses:

1- Manifestations of God's kindness and good management in His creation.

2- Manifestations of God's honouring and kindness to His servant and messenger Moses, peace be upon him.

3- A sign of God's love for Moses, and its effect in people's love for him.

4- Affirmation of the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ) through his informing, in his Book, of such events in the stories of Moses, peace be upon him.

It has already been mentioned that Moses, peace be upon him, asked his Lord for matters to serve as a help to him in bearing his message, and the Exalted answered him with His saying, in this verse [36]: ﴿He said: You have been granted your request, O Moses﴾, that is, what you asked for has been given to you. ﴿And We had already bestowed favour upon you another time﴾, that is, before these requests, when Pharaoh commanded the slaughter of the sons of the Children of Israel, ﴿when We inspired your mother with what was inspired, saying: Cast him into the chest﴾, that is, into the box, ﴿then cast him into the river﴾, that is, the Nile, ﴿and the river will throw him onto the bank, and there will take him an enemy of Mine and an enemy of his﴾. This deliverance is a blessing, and another blessing is contained in His saying: ﴿And I cast upon you love from Me﴾, that is, I bestowed upon you My love, so whoever saw you would love you. Another blessing is: so that you might be raised and nourished under My sight and by My will, I returned you by My arrangement to your mother so that she would nurse you, her eye would be comforted, and she would not grieve over your separation. This is what His saying contains: ﴿When your sister walked and said: Shall I direct you to one who will take charge of him?﴾, that is, for you, for his nursing and rearing. ﴿So We returned you to your mother that her eye might be comforted and she not grieve﴾. Another blessing, and the greatest, is Our deliverance of you from the great distress after you killed a soul and the family of Pharaoh conspired to kill you: ﴿So We delivered you from distress﴾, from killing, and We forgave you the sin of killing. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We tested you with many trials﴾, that is, We afflicted you with a great affliction. Here is its summary in the following points:

1- Your mother's bearing you in the year in which the sons of the Children of Israel were being slain.

2- Your mother casting you into the river.

3- The forbidding of wet-nurses to you until you returned to your mother.

4- Your seizing Pharaoh's beard and his intent to kill you.

5- Your killing of the Copt and the conspiracy of Pharaoh's family to kill you.

6- Your residence in Midian and what you endured of the pains of estrangement.

7- Your losing your way with your family and what befell you of fear and fatigue.

These are some of what falls under His saying: ﴿And We tested you with many trials﴾, and His saying: ﴿Then you stayed for years among the people of Midian﴾, pasturing the sheep of Shuʿayb for ten years, ﴿then you came﴾ from Midian to Mount Sinai ﴿at an appointed time﴾ decreed by Us, a determined promise that you did not know until you met it.

*Wa-iṣṭanaʿtuka li-nafsī*, that is, I created you, reared you, tested you, and brought you at an appointed time I had decreed, to charge you with the burden of the message to Pharaoh and the Children of Israel: to Pharaoh, to call him to worship Us and to send the Children of Israel with you to the land of return; and to the Children of Israel, to guide and reform them and prepare them for happiness and perfection in both abodes, if they believe and remain upright.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 20, verse 42–48:

Explanation of the words:

*Bi-ayati* (with My signs): that is, with the miracles I gave you, such as the staff, the hand, and others.

*Wa la tanyā fī dhikri* (and do not slacken in My remembrance): that is, do not weaken or fall short in remembering Me, for it is the secret of life and your help in carrying out your mission.

*Innahu taghā* (he has transgressed): he exceeded his station by claiming divinity and lordship.

*Qawlan layyinan* (gentle speech): that is, free from harshness and violence.

*La'allahu yatadhakkaru* (perhaps he will be mindful): that is, through what you say he may come to know Us, and thus fear Us, and so believe, submit, and send the Children of Israel with you.

*Yafruta 'alaynā* (he may hasten against us): that is, he may hasten our punishment before We call him and make things clear to him.

*Aw an yaṭghā* (or that he may increase in transgression): that is, he may grow greater in tyranny and wrongdoing.

*Asma'u wa ara* (I hear and I see): that is, I hear what you say and what is said to you, and I see what you do and what is done to you.

*Fa-arsil ma'anā Banī Isrā'īl* (so send with us the Children of Israel): that is, that we may take them to the Promised Land, the land of their forefather Abraham.

*Bi-āyah* (with a sign): that is, a miracle proving the truth of our call, and that we are truly and sincerely the messengers of your Lord.

*Wa'l-salāmu 'alā man ittaba'a'l-hudā* (and peace is upon those who follow guidance): that is, deliverance from punishment in both abodes for those who believe and fear God, since guidance is faith and piety.

*Man kadhdhaba wa tawallā* (whoever denies and turns away): that is, whoever denies the truth and its call and turns away from both, not accepting them.

Explanation of the meanings:

The noble context continues its discussion of Moses with his Lord, blessed and exalted. In the previous verse He informed him that He had made him for Himself. In this verse He commands him to go with his brother Aaron, equipped with the signs of God, which are the proofs He had given them: the staff and the white hand. He forbade them from slackening in the remembrance of God, that is, from weakening in remembering His promise and His threat, which would cause them to fall short in calling to Him, exalted is He. He said: ﴿Go, you and your brother, with My signs, and do not slacken in My remembrance﴾. He made clear to them to whom they should go and why, saying: ﴿Go to Pharaoh; he has indeed transgressed﴾, meaning he has exceeded his station and overstepped his limit, from a man who worships God to a disbelieving man who claimed to be a lord and a god. He taught them the method of calling, saying to them: ﴿Speak to him with gentle speech﴾, meaning free from harshness, roughness, and bad manner. He gave the reason for this, saying: ﴿Perhaps he will be mindful or fear﴾, meaning in hope that he will reflect on the meanings of your words and what you call him to, so that he reconsiders himself, believes, and is guided, or fears the punishment if he remains in his disbelief and wrongdoing, and so submits to you and sends the Children of Israel with you. Moses and his brother Aaron expressed apprehension, as God related about them in His saying: ﴿They said: Our Lord, we fear that he will hasten against us﴾, meaning that he will hasten our punishment by beating or killing, ﴿or that he will increase in transgression﴾, meaning grow greater in tyranny and wrongdoing. Their Lord, mighty and majestic, reassured them that He was with them through His help, support, and guidance to all that is in their honor, and said to them: ﴿Do not fear﴾, meaning of Pharaoh and his chiefs. ﴿Indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see﴾: I hear what you say to Pharaoh and what he says to you, and I see what you do and what Pharaoh does, and I will support you against him, validate your deed and nullify his. So go to him and do not hesitate. Say to him, that is, to Pharaoh: ﴿We are two messengers of your Lord﴾, that is, sent to you, ﴿so send with us the Children of Israel﴾, that we may bring them out where God has commanded, ﴿and do not torment them﴾ by killing their men, sparing their women, and employing them in the worst and most degrading tasks. ﴿We have indeed brought you a sign from your Lord﴾, that is, a proof from your Lord showing that we are the messengers of your Lord to you, and that He commands you to justice and monotheism and forbids you from wrongdoing and disbelief, and that you must not prevent the Children of Israel from leaving with us for the Promised Land. ﴿And peace is upon him who follows guidance﴾: that is, know, O Pharaoh, that security and safety are attained by those who follow the guidance we have brought you; so follow the guidance and you will be safe, otherwise you are exposed to fears, destruction, and ruin. This is because ﴿it has been revealed to us﴾, that is, our Lord has revealed to us, ﴿that the punishment is upon him who denies﴾ the truth we have brought you ﴿and turns away﴾ from it, refusing to accept it out of arrogance and obstinacy.

Guidance from the verses:

1. The great importance of remembrance of God with the heart, the tongue, and the limbs, that is, through obedience in action and in abstention.
2. The obligation to observe wisdom in calling people to their Lord.
3. Affirmation of God's presence with His friends and righteous servants, by helping and supporting them.
4. Affirmation that safety from the punishment of this world and the Hereafter belongs to those who follow guidance.
5. The legitimacy of approaching a wrongdoer, commanding and forbidding him, and enduring his harm.
6. Not being held accountable for fear where its causes exist.

Guidance from the verses:

1. The great importance of remembrance of God with the heart, the tongue, and the limbs, that is, through obedience in action and in abstention.
2. The obligation to observe wisdom in calling people to their Lord.
3. Affirmation of God's presence with His friends and righteous servants, by helping and supporting them.
4. Affirmation that safety from the punishment of this world and the Hereafter belongs to those who follow guidance.
5. The legitimacy of approaching a wrongdoer, commanding and forbidding him, and enduring his harm.
6. Not being held accountable for fear where its causes exist.

Explanation of the words:

"In a Book. My Lord neither errs nor forgets": i.e., the deeds of those nations are in a preserved Book with my Lord, and He will recompense them for their deeds. Indeed my Lord does not err or forget. If He punishes or delays the punishment, that is for a wisdom He has decreed.

"A bed, and has threaded for you therein roads": "a bed" means a couch or spread; "threaded" means made easy; "roads" means paths.

"Pairs of various plants": "pairs" means kinds; "various" means differing in colors and tastes.

"Indeed in that are signs": i.e., clear proofs of God's power, knowledge, wisdom and mercy.

"For people of intellect": i.e., people of reason. The word "nuhā" (intellect) refers to reason, and it was so named because it restrains its possessor from committing abominations such as polytheism and sins.

"From it We created you": i.e., from the earth, and into it We will return you after death, and from it We will bring you out at the Resurrection on the Day of Judgment.

"And once again": i.e., another time, since the first was creation from the clay of the earth, and this is bringing forth from the earth.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context is the dialogue that took place between Moses, peace be upon him, and Pharaoh, when Moses and his brother arrived at Pharaoh and called him to God, Exalted, to believe in Him and worship Him, in a calm and gentle manner as God had commanded them. They said to him: ﴿And peace be upon him who follows guidance. Indeed it has been revealed to us that the punishment is upon him who denies and turns away﴾ [Ta-Ha: 47–48], and they did not say to him, "There is no peace upon you," nor "You are a denier and will be punished." Here Pharaoh said to them what God related in His words: ﴿He said: Who then is your Lord, O Moses?﴾ The accursed one singled out Moses by mention, because of Moses' claim to him through the blessing of being raised in his house, and because he was the first messenger. Moses answered him with what God related in His words: ﴿Our Lord is He who gave everything its creation, then guided﴾, meaning every created thing was given its creation, the form it has, distinguished by its shape, color, attributes and essence; then He guided the living among His creatures to seek their provision of food and drink, and to seek their survival by what He instituted for them and guided them to, namely the ways of reproduction, to preserve their species. Here, when Moses had silenced Pharaoh and cut off his argument with what God had inspired him of knowledge and clarity, Pharaoh, diverting Moses from the goal out of fear of disgrace before his chiefs and of defeat, said: ﴿So what of the former generations?﴾, i.e., tell us about the people of Noah, Hud and Salih, who used to worship idols. Moses realized that the accursed one wanted to divert him from the truth, so he said to him what God related in His words: ﴿Its knowledge is with my Lord, in a Book. My Lord neither errs nor forgets﴾. What you asked about does not concern us. The condition of those past nations is known to my Lord, in a preserved tablet with Him, and He will recompense them for their deeds. Whatever punishment He hastened for them or delayed is only for a wisdom He knows, for my Lord neither errs nor forgets, and He will recompense every soul according to what it earned.

Then Moses began to describe his Lord and make Him known to them, seizing the opportunity that had presented itself, and he said: ﴿Who made the earth for you a bed﴾, i.e., a spread on which life is lived; ﴿and threaded for you therein roads﴾, i.e., He made easy for you the paths upon it, by which you can travel and reach your needs; ﴿and sent down from the sky water﴾, which is the rain that forms the rivers and nourishes and feeds the wells. This is my Lord and your Lord, so know Him, worship Him, and do not worship anything besides Him. God's words: ﴿Then We brought forth thereby pairs of various plants﴾, i.e., by the rain, pairs, meaning kinds, of various plants, meaning differing in colors, tastes, scents and properties. This was part of God's speech completing Moses' words and a reminder to the people of Makkah who were heedless of God and of His right to monotheism. His words: ﴿Eat and graze your livestock﴾, i.e., of what We have mentioned to you of the pairs of plants, and graze your camels, sheep and all your cattle, and give thanks to Us for this bounty by worshipping Us and abandoning the worship of others. His words, Exalted: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for people of intellect﴾, i.e., indeed in that mentioned, the sending down of rain and the growing of plants to feed humans and animals, are proofs of God's power, knowledge, wisdom and mercy, and that by this He alone deserves worship to the exclusion of anything else. However, these proofs are understood only by people of reason and possessors of intellect, who are the ones who derive guidance from them to the knowledge of God, the obligation to worship Him, and the abandonment of worshipping others. His words, Exalted: ﴿From it We created you﴾, i.e., from the earth in which plant and animal life exists, by creating your first ancestor, Adam; ﴿and into it We return you﴾ by death, so that you are buried alive for reckoning and for recompense, with eternal bliss or humiliating punishment according to the qualities of your souls. The one with a pure soul will be blessed, and the one with an evil soul, through polytheism and sins, will be punished.

Lessons from the verses:

1- It is required to answer the questioner, and the answer should be with sound and beneficial knowledge.

2- Establishing the principle that part of the goodness of a person's Islam is leaving what does not concern him.

3- Exalting the Lord, Exalted, above error and forgetfulness.

4- Deriving proof from the cosmic signs for the Creator, Mighty and Majestic, His power and His divinity.

5- Respecting and honoring the intellect, for it restrains its possessor from falsehood and evil.

6- Naming the intellect "nuhā" because it restrains its possessor from abominations.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 20, verse 56–60:

Explanation of the words:

"Arayناhu ayatina kullaha" (We showed him all Our signs): i.e., We let him see Our proofs and evidences of the truth of what We sent Our two messengers, Musa and Harun, to him with, all of them. He rejected them and refused to believe that they were two messengers to him from the Lord of the worlds.

"Min ardina" (from our land): i.e., the land of Egypt, over which Fir'awn (Pharaoh) was king.

"Bisihrika ya Musa" (with your magic, O Musa): this refers to the staff and the white hand.

"Makanan siwa" (a place equidistant): i.e., a place of justice between us and you, and of equal standing, suitable for the contest, such that it is a great open, level arena where everyone who looks at it can see what takes place in it.

"Yawm al-zinah" (the Day of Adornment): i.e., a festival day on which they adorn themselves and abstain from work.

"Wa an yuhsha al-nas duha" (and that the people be gathered in the forenoon): i.e., and that the people be brought from all parts of the land to watch the contest.

"Fatawla Fir'awn" (then Fir'awn turned away): i.e., he withdrew from the council of debate between him and Musa and Harun, in arrogance and aversion.

"Fajama'a kaydahu" (then he gathered his scheme): i.e., he mustered his power and his magicians.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with the dialogue between Musa and Harun on one side and Fir'awn and his chiefs on the other. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We indeed showed him Our signs, all of them﴾, i.e., We showed Fir'awn Our proofs and evidences that Musa and Harun are two messengers sent by Us to him. But he denied their messengership and refused to acknowledge them, and said what Allah the Exalted related of him: ﴿He said: "Have you come to us, O Musa, to drive us out of our land﴾, i.e., our dwellings, our homes and our kingdom, ﴿by your magic?﴾ — the magic by which your staff became a moving serpent. ﴿So we will surely bring you magic like it. So appoint between us and you a appointment which neither we nor you will fail to keep, at a place equidistant﴾, a fair place between us and you, of such moderation and spaciousness that everyone who looks at it sees what takes place in the contest between us and you. Musa replied with what Allah the Exalted related of him, saying: ﴿Your appointment is the Day of Adornment﴾, which is a festival day for the Copts, on which they beautify themselves and abstain from work, ﴿and that the people be gathered in the forenoon﴾, i.e., on a day when the people are gathered in the forenoon to watch the contest from all parts of the kingdom. Here "tawalla Fir'awn" means he turned away from the council of debate, full of arrogance and obstinacy, and gathered his forces of magicians to carry out his scheme against Musa and Harun. In the following verses the truth will appear.

Guidance of the verses:

1- Demonstration of Fir'awn's arrogance, insolence and tyranny.

2- Magic has effects, and it has schools in which it is taught, and men who master it and teach it.

3- The legitimacy of a duel and contest to manifest the truth and nullify falsehood.

4- The legitimacy of choosing the suitable place and time for battle, contest and the like.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 20, verses 67–71:

Explanation of the words:

﴿فأوجس في نفسه خيفة﴾: That is, he sensed fear within himself.

﴿أنت الأعلى﴾: That is, the dominant, the victorious.

﴿تلقف﴾: That is, it swallows up quickly what the magicians have made of those ropes and staffs.

﴿كيد ساحر﴾: That is, the scheme of magic that has no permanence and no stability.

﴿لا يفلح الساحر﴾: That is, the magician does not attain his goal wherever he may be.

﴿فألقي السحرة سجداً﴾: That is, they cast themselves down, with their heads, upon the ground, prostrating.

﴿إنه لكبيركم﴾: That is, your teacher who taught you magic.

﴿من خلاف﴾: That is, a right hand with a left foot.

﴿في جذوع النخل﴾: That is, upon the trunks of date palms.

﴿أينا أشد عذاباً وأبقى﴾: He means himself, may Allah curse him, and the Lord of Musa, who is more severe in punishment and more lasting in it for opposing and disobeying Him.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to speak of the contest between Musa (peace be upon him) and the magicians of Pharaoh. When the magicians threw their ropes and staffs, and they moved, convulsed, and filled the arena with them, Musa felt fear within himself. Then his Lord, exalted is He, revealed to him at that very moment: ﴿Fear not, indeed you are the superior,﴾ that is, the dominant, the overpowering over them.

This is what the first verse [67] indicates: ﴿So Musa sensed fear within himself﴾, and the second [68]: ﴿We said, "Fear not; indeed, you are the superior."﴾ And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And throw what is in your right hand; it will swallow up what they have made﴾, that is, it will swallow quickly. He gave the reason for that, saying: ﴿What they have made is only the scheme of a magician﴾, that is, it is deception and trickery from a magician, ﴿and the magician does not succeed wherever he comes﴾, that is, the magician does not win what he wants nor ever attain it, because it is merely illusions that he shows to others, having no firm reality that does not change.

When the magicians witnessed the staff swallowing all their ropes and staffs, they knew that what Musa had brought was not magic but a heavenly miracle. They cast themselves down upon the ground, prostrating to Allah, Lord of the worlds, because the greatness of the miracle had overwhelmed their souls, and they said plainly: ﴿We have believed in the Lord of Harun and Musa.﴾ Here Pharaoh cried out, roaring and threatening, so that he might avert in his own view the evil of defeat, and he said to the magicians: ﴿Have you believed in him before I give you permission?﴾ ﴿Indeed, he is your chief who taught you magic﴾, that is, your great teacher ﴿who taught you magic,﴾ so you colluded with him in the defeat. ﴿I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on alternate sides﴾, as torture and exemplary punishment, so cut off the right hand of one of you with the left foot, or the reverse, ﴿and I will surely crucify you upon the trunks of date palms﴾, that is, I will fasten you upon date-palm trunks and leave you hanging as a lesson and a deterrent to others, ﴿and you will surely know whose punishment is more severe and more lasting﴾, that is, more enduring: the Lord of Musa, in whom you have believed, or I, Pharaoh, upon whom be the curses of Allah.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Feeling fear and sensing it upon witnessing its causes does not detract from faith.

2- Affirmation that what the magicians display of transforming one thing into another is merely imagination with no reality.

3- The prohibition of magic, because it is fabrication and deception.

4- The strong effect of the miracle upon the souls of the magicians, because of the difference they perceived between the sign and magic.

5- The courage of the believer, whom fear of killing or crucifixion does not terrify.

﴿كيد ساحر﴾: That is, the scheme of magic that has no permanence and no stability.

﴿لا يفلح الساحر﴾: That is, the magician does not attain his goal wherever he may be.

﴿فألقي السحرة سجداً﴾: That is, they cast themselves down, with their heads, upon the ground, prostrating.

﴿إنه لكبيركم﴾: That is, your teacher who taught you magic.

﴿من خلاف﴾: That is, a right hand with a left foot.

﴿في جذوع النخل﴾: That is, upon the trunks of date palms.

﴿أينا أشد عذاباً وأبقى﴾: He means himself, may Allah curse him, and the Lord of Musa, who is more severe in punishment and more lasting in it for opposing and disobeying Him.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to speak of the contest between Musa (peace be upon him) and the magicians of Pharaoh. When the magicians threw their ropes and staffs, and they moved, convulsed, and filled the arena with them, Musa felt fear within himself. Then his Lord, exalted is He, revealed to him at that very moment: ﴿Fear not, indeed you are the superior,﴾ that is, the dominant, the overpowering over them.

This is what the first verse [67] indicates: ﴿So Musa sensed fear within himself﴾, and the second [68]: ﴿We said, "Fear not; indeed, you are the superior."﴾ And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And throw what is in your right hand; it will swallow up what they have made﴾, that is, it will swallow quickly. He gave the reason for that, saying: ﴿What they have made is only the scheme of a magician﴾, that is, it is deception and trickery from a magician, ﴿and the magician does not succeed wherever he comes﴾, that is, the magician does not win what he wants nor ever attain it, because it is merely illusions that he shows to others, having no firm reality that does not change.

When the magicians witnessed the staff swallowing all their ropes and staffs, they knew that what Musa had brought was not magic but a heavenly miracle. They cast themselves down upon the ground, prostrating to Allah, Lord of the worlds, because the greatness of the miracle had overwhelmed their souls, and they said plainly: ﴿We have believed in the Lord of Harun and Musa.﴾ Here Pharaoh cried out, roaring and threatening, so that he might avert in his own view the evil of defeat, and he said to the magicians: ﴿Have you believed in him before I give you permission?﴾ ﴿Indeed, he is your chief who taught you magic﴾, that is, your great teacher ﴿who taught you magic,﴾ so you colluded with him in the defeat. ﴿I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on alternate sides﴾, as torture and exemplary punishment, so cut off the right hand of one of you with the left foot, or the reverse, ﴿and I will surely crucify you upon the trunks of date palms﴾, that is, I will fasten you upon date-palm trunks and leave you hanging as a lesson and a deterrent to others, ﴿and you will surely know whose punishment is more severe and more lasting﴾, that is, more enduring: the Lord of Musa, in whom you have believed, or I, Pharaoh, upon whom be the curses of Allah.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Feeling fear and sensing it upon witnessing its causes does not detract from faith.

2- Affirmation that what the magicians display of transforming one thing into another is merely imagination with no reality.

3- The prohibition of magic, because it is fabrication and deception.

4- The strong effect of the miracle upon the souls of the magicians, because of the difference they perceived between the sign and magic.

5- The courage of the believer, whom fear of killing or crucifixion does not terrify.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 20, verses 72–76:

Explanation of the words:

Lan nu'thiraka (لن نؤثرك): That is, we will not prefer you and choose you.

Wal-ladhi fatharana (والذي فطرنا): That is, the One who created us when we were nothing.

Faqḍi ma anta qadin (فاقض ما أنت قاض): That is, do what you said you would do to us.

Wallahu khayrun wa abqa (والله خير وأبقى): That is, better in reward for the one who obeys Him, and more lasting in punishment for the one who disobeys Him, than you.

Mujriman (مجرما): Mujriman means one who is a criminal against himself, corrupting himself with the effects of shirk, disbelief and sins.

Jaza'u man tazakka (جزاء من تزكى): That is, the reward of the one who purifies himself from the effects of shirk and sins, through faith and righteous deeds.

Meaning of the verses:

The context remains with Pharaoh and the believing sorcerers. When Pharaoh threatened them with death and crucifixion on the trunks of palm trees because of their faith in God and their disbelief in him, for he was the tyrant, they said to him what God the Exalted reports about them in this verse [72]: ﴿They said, "We will never prefer you over the clear proofs that have come to us"﴾, O Pharaoh, ﴿over the One who created us.﴾ The proofs and conclusive arguments that the Lord of Moses and Aaron is the true Lord, whose worship and obedience are obligatory. So we will not choose you over the One who created us, to believe in you and disbelieve in Him. This will never happen. ﴿So decree whatever you are going to decree.﴾ Of killing and crucifixion against us. ﴿You only decree concerning this worldly life.﴾ In this worldly life, because of the authority you have in it. As for the Hereafter, you will be judged in it to abide in humiliating punishment.

They affirmed their faith without fear or trembling, saying: ﴿Indeed, we have believed in our Lord﴾, that is, our Creator, our Provider and the Manager of our affairs, ﴿that He may forgive us our sins﴾, that is, our wrongdoings, ﴿and what you compelled us to do of magic﴾, that is, learning it and practising it, while we do not want that. There is no doubt that Pharaoh had obliged them to learn magic and practise it in order to fight Moses and Aaron, because of what he saw of the miracle of the staff and the hand. Their saying ﴿And Allah is better and more lasting﴾ means: better in reward and good recompense for the one who believes in Him and does righteous deeds, and more lasting in punishment for the one who disbelieves in Him, believes in other than Him and disobeys Him. This is what the two verses [72] and [73] indicate.

As for the third verse [74], which is His saying: ﴿Indeed, whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal﴾, that is, against himself by corrupting it with shirk and sins, ﴿indeed, for him is Hell; he will neither die therein nor live.﴾ So he is not relieved of punishment therein, ﴿nor [does he] live﴾, a life in which he is happy.

Their saying ﴿And whoever comes to Him as a believer who has done righteous deeds﴾, that is, a believer in Him, a disbeliever in the tyrant, who has acted by His laws, performing the obligations and avoiding the prohibitions, ﴿those will have the highest ranks﴾ as the reward of their faith and righteous deeds, ﴿gardens of perpetual residence, beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever.﴾ They will not die nor leave them. ﴿And that is the reward of those who purify themselves﴾, that is, who purify themselves through faith and righteous deeds after abandoning shirk, sins and wrongdoings. There is no doubt that this knowledge which the sorcerers had was acquired through the call of Moses and Aaron, for they had remained among them for a long time.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Disbelief does not prevail over faith, nor falsehood over truth, nor superstition over the correct religion, except by a foolish ignorant person.

2- Establishing the principle that the punishment of this world is endured and borne with patience in view of the punishment of the Hereafter.

3- Coercion is of two kinds: that which is by beating that cannot be endured is forgiven to its victim; and that which is merely by threat and demand, which is not forgiven except by sincere repentance. The coercion of the sorcerers was of the second kind.

4- Explanation of the recompense of each of disbelief and sins, and of faith and righteous deeds, in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 20, verses 77–82:

Explanation of the words:

"أن أسر بعبادي" (Asri bi-ibadi, "Travel by night with My servants"): i.e., travel by night from the land of Egypt.

"طريقاً في البحر يبساً" (a dry path in the sea): i.e., a dry path in the middle of the sea, with no water in it.

"لا تخاف دركاً" (Do not fear being overtaken): i.e., do not fear that Pharaoh will overtake you, and do not fear drowning.

"فغشيهم من اليم" (Then the sea covered them): i.e., it covered them with the water of the sea, such that they drowned in it.

"وأضل فرعون قومه" (And Pharaoh led his people astray): i.e., by calling them to belief in him and to disbelief in God, Lord of the worlds.

"وما هدى" (And he did not guide them): i.e., he did not guide them as he had promised with his words: ﴿And I only show you the path of right judgment﴾ [Ghafir: 29].

"جانب الطور الأيمن" (the right side of Mount Sinai): i.e., for the purpose of giving Moses the Torah, which contains the order of their lives in both religion and worldly affairs.

"المن والسلوى" (the manna and the quail): al-Mann is a white thing like snow, and al-Salwa is a bird known as the quail (al-Sammani).

"ولا تطغوا فيه" (And do not transgress therein): i.e., by excess in it, and by failing to thank God for it.

"ثم اهتدى" (then remains guided): i.e., by steadfastness upon faith, monotheism and righteous deeds until death.

Meaning of the verses:

After the long dispute and fierce contention that lasted a considerable time, in which Pharaoh and his people refused to accept the truth and submit to it, God, Exalted, revealed to Moses, peace be upon him, what He informs of in His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And We had already revealed to Moses﴾, and what He revealed to him: to travel by night with the Children of Israel. This is His words, Exalted: ﴿And We had already revealed to Moses, "Travel by night with My servants"﴾. His words ﴿So strike for them a dry path in the sea﴾ mean: make for them a path through the middle of the sea. This was accomplished after he struck the sea with his staff, and the sea split into two parts, and the path through its middle was dry with no water in it, until the Children of Israel crossed the sea. When Pharaoh followed them and entered the sea with his armies, God, Exalted, closed the sea over them and drowned them all, after He had saved Moses and the Children of Israel. This is the meaning of His words, Exalted: ﴿Then Pharaoh followed them with his soldiers, and there covered them of the sea that which covered them﴾, i.e., of the water of the sea, ﴿that which covered them﴾, i.e., the great thing of the waters of the sea. His words to Moses ﴿Do not fear being overtaken, nor be afraid﴾ mean: do not fear that Pharaoh will overtake you from behind, and do not fear drowning in the sea.

His words, Exalted: ﴿And Pharaoh led his people astray, and did not guide them﴾ are a statement from Him, Exalted, that Pharaoh led his followers astray, since he deprived them of faith in the truth and of following its path, and called them to disbelief in the truth and to avoiding its path. 2- The sign of the splitting of the sea and the existence of a dry path in it for the Children of Israel, until they crossed it, shows God's generosity, power, knowledge, mercy and wisdom.

3- A reminder to the Jews contemporary with the Islamic call of God's favour upon their predecessors, so that they may give thanks, repent, and submit.

4- The prohibition of excess and wrongdoing, and of ingratitude for blessings.

5- Wrath is an attribute of God, Exalted, as befits His majesty and perfection, not the attributes of created beings.

**Explanation of the words:**

**Wa ma a'jalaka:** What made you hasten away from your people, meaning what made you leave your people and come ahead of them.

**Hum ala athari:** They are coming after me and are not far from me.

**Wa 'ajiltu ilayka Rabbi li-tarda:** I hastened to come to You seeking Your pleasure with me.

**Qad fatanna qawmaka:** We tested your people, meaning We put them to trial by worshipping the calf.

**Wa adallahumu al-Samiri:** He led them away from guidance, which is Islam, into shirk (associating partners with God) and the worship of other than the Lord, exalted is He.

**Ghadban asifan:** Extremely angry and grieved.

**Wa'dan hasanan:** That He would give you the Torah (the revealed scripture of Moses), which contains the order of your lives and the law of your Lord, so that you might complete your lives upon it and be happy.

**Afatala 'alaykumu al-'ahd:** The period of the appointment, which was thirty days, before God completed it to forty days.

**Bi-mulkina:** By our command and our capacity. However, desire overcame us, and we were unable to fulfil the promise of following you.

**Awzaran:** Loads of the jewelry and garments of the women of the Copts (the Egyptians).

**Faqadhafnaha:** We threw them into the pit by the command of Harun (peace be upon him).

**Alqa al-Samiri:** Al-Samiri is Musa ibn Dhafar from the Israelite tribe of Samira. What he cast was the dust he had taken from under the hoof of Jibril's horse; he cast it onto the jewelry.

**'Ijlan jasadan:** A body with a physical form.

**Lahu khuwar:** Khuwar is the sound of a cow.

**Fa-nasiya:** That is, Musa forgot his Lord here and went off to seek Him.

**Ala yarji'u ilayhim qawla:** That it does not speak to them when they address it, because it cannot utter anything except lowing.

**Ma'na al-ayat (The meaning of the verses):**

After God saved the Children of Israel from Pharaoh and his chiefs, when Musa led them across the sea and God drowned Pharaoh and his soldiers, Musa informed them that his Lord had commanded him to come to Him with the Children of Israel, who were on their way to the Promised Land, at Mount Tur, to give them the Torah, which contains their law and the order of their lives in this world and the next. He had promised them the right side of Mount Tur. Musa hastened on the way to the appointment and appointed his brother Harun over the Children of Israel, so that he could lead them behind Musa slowly until they caught up with him at Mount Tur. It happened that al-Samiri tested the Children of Israel with the calf, invited them to worship it, and made them abandon following Musa (peace be upon him). Therefore, the words of God, ﹤﻿﻿ ﴿وَمَا أَعْجَلَكَ عَن قَوْمِكَ يَا مُوسَىٰ﴾ ﴾ ("And what hastened you away from your people, O Musa?"), are a question from God to Musa to inform him of what happened to his people after him, although He knew it already. When God said to Musa, "And what hastened you," about coming alone without the Children of Israel, even though the matter was that you were to come with them, Musa answered, ﴿هُمْ أُولَاءِ عَلَىٰ أَثَرِي﴾ ("They are right behind me"), meaning they are coming after me, and "I hastened to You, my Lord, that You may be pleased with me." Here God informed him of what had happened to his people, saying, mighty and majestic is He, ﴿فَإِنَّا قَدْ فَتَنَّا قَوْمَكَ مِن بَعْدِكَ وَأَضَلَّهُمُ السَّامِرِيُّ﴾ ("Indeed We have tested your people after you, and al-Samiri has led them astray"), meaning by making the calf for them and inviting them to worship it, on the pretext that it was the Lord, exalted is He, and that Musa had failed to find Him. When the private conference ended and God gave Musa the tablets containing the Torah, ﴿فَرَجَعَ مُوسَىٰ إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِ غَضْبَانَ أَسِفًا﴾ ("So Musa returned to his people, angry and grieved"), meaning he returned to his people grieved. He said to them, regarding what God had told him, ﴿قَالَ يَا قَوْمِ أَلَمْ يَعِدْكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ وَعْدًا حَسَنًا﴾ ("He said, 'O my people, did your Lord not make you a good promise?'"). He reminded them of God's promise to save them from the family of Pharaoh and to honour them with sovereignty and leadership, rebuking them for their sin of lagging behind him, their preoccupation with worshipping the calf, and the serious disputes among them. His words, ﴿أَفَطَالَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْعَهْدُ﴾ ("Did the period seem long to you?"), mean it was not long; the period was thirty days, and it had not been completed before you were tested and worshipped other than God, exalted is He. His words, ﴿أَمْ أَرَدتُّمْ أَن يَحِلَّ عَلَيْكُمْ غَضَبٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ﴾ ("Or did you wish that wrath from your Lord should descend upon you?"), mean: rather, you wished by your corrupt action that wrath from your Lord should become due upon you, and it descended upon you. ﴿فَأَخْلَفْتُم مَّوْعِدِي﴾ ("So you broke your appointment with me"), by devoting yourselves to worshipping the calf and abandoning following me to attend the appointment of the Lord, exalted is He, which He had promised you.

His words, exalted is He, ﴿قَالُوا مَا أَخْلَفْنَا مَوْعِدَكَ بِمَلْكِنَا﴾ ("They said, 'We did not break our appointment with you by our own power'"), are what the people of Musa said as excuse-makers to him. They claimed they were unable to avoid breaking the appointment, because desire overcame them, so they could not endure following him while the calf existed and al-Samiri had misled them, saying it was their god and that Musa had mistaken the way to Him. This is the meaning of their words, ﴿مَا أَخْلَفْنَا مَوْعِدَكَ بِمَلْكِنَا﴾, meaning by our command and our power, since we were overpowered in our own affairs.

Their words, ﴿وَلَٰكِنَّا حُمِّلْنَا أَوْزَارًا مِّن زِينَةِ الْقَوْمِ فَقَذَفْنَاهَا﴾ ("But we were laden with burdens of the people's ornaments, so we threw them [in]"), explain the cause and reason for the test. When they were leaving Egypt, their women borrowed jewelry from the women of the Copts on the pretext of a festival for them. In the morning they set out with Musa on their way to al-Quds (Jerusalem), and their deliverance and the drowning of Pharaoh were completed. When they camped on the coast, Musa hastened to his Lord's appointment and left them under the command of his brother Harun, on condition that they continue their journey behind Musa to Mount Tur. However, Musa, who was nicknamed al-Samiri, seized the opportunity and said to the women of the Children of Israel, "The jewelry you have does not lawfully belong to you, since it is a trust. How can you consider it lawful?" He dug a pit for them and said, "Throw it in there," and he lit a fire in it so that it would burn and could no longer be used. This is what their words indicate: ﴿وَلَٰكِنَّا حُمِّلْنَا أَوْزَارًا مِّن زِينَةِ الْقَوْمِ﴾, meaning the people of Pharaoh. So we threw them, meaning into the pit that al-Samiri had commanded.

His words, exalted is He, ﴿فَكَذَٰلِكَ أَلْقَى السَّامِرِيُّ﴾ ("So thus al-Samiri cast [it]"), are part of the speech of the Children of Israel to Musa. Just as we threw the jewelry into the pit, al-Samiri threw what he had of the dust that he had taken from under the hoof of Jibril's horse. Al-Samiri made the calf and brought it out for them as a body with a form that had a lowing sound. Some of them said to others, "This is your god and the god of Musa, who went to his appointment and forgot, and lost the way to Him, so worship it until Musa comes back." God said, rebuking them, ﴿أَفَلَا يَرَوْنَ أَلَّا يَرْجِعُ إِلَيْهِمْ قَوْلًا﴾ ("Do they not see that it does not return to them any word?"), when they address it, ﴿وَلَا يَمْلِكُ لَهُمْ ضَرًّا وَلَا نَفْعًا﴾ ("and it has no power to harm or benefit them"). How could they think it is a god when it does not answer them when they ask it, does not give them when they request, and does not help them when they seek help? It was ignorance, misguidance, and following desire. We seek refuge in God, exalted is He.

**Guidance from the verses (Hidayat al-ayat):**

1. Condemnation of haste and an explanation of its harmful effects. Musa's hastening to the appointment and leaving his people behind him was the cause of a great matter, namely the worship of the calf, and the grave consequences that followed from it.

2. The legitimacy of seeking God's pleasure, provided it is through what He loves to be drawn near to Him by.

3. The legitimacy of anger for God and grief over abandoning His worship by violating His command and prohibition.

4. The legitimacy of women borrowing jewelry and adornments, and the prohibition of denying or taking them wrongfully.

5. The obligation to use reason and to apply thought in distinguishing truth from falsehood, and good from evil.

3. The legitimacy of anger for God and grief over abandoning His worship by violating His command and prohibition.

4. The legitimacy of women borrowing jewelry and adornments, and the prohibition of denying or taking them wrongfully.

5. The obligation to use reason and to apply thought in distinguishing truth from falsehood, and good from evil.

**Explanation of the words:**

**Hum ala athari:** They are coming after me and are not far from me.

**Wa 'ajiltu ilayka Rabbi li-tarda:** I hastened to come to You seeking Your pleasure with me.

**Qad fatanna qawmaka:** We tested your people, meaning We put them to trial by worshipping the calf.

**Wa adallahumu al-Samiri:** He led them away from guidance, which is Islam, into shirk (associating partners with God) and the worship of other than the Lord, exalted is He.

**Ghadban asifan:** Extremely angry and grieved.

**Wa'dan hasanan:** That He would give you the Torah (the revealed scripture of Moses), which contains the order of your lives and the law of your Lord, so that you might complete your lives upon it and be happy.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 20, verses 90–94:

Explanation of the words:

Futintum bihi (فتنتم به): i.e., you were tested by it, namely by the calf.

Lan nabraha 'alayhi 'akifin (لن نبرح عليه عاكفين): i.e., we will not cease remaining devoted to its worship.

Idh ra'aytahum dallu (إذ رأيتهم ضلوا): i.e., by worshipping the calf and taking it as a god besides Allah, exalted is He.

La ta'khudh bi-lihyati (لا تأخذ بلحيتي): where Musa, out of intense anger, seized his brother's beard and head-hair and dragged him toward himself, rebuking him and blaming him for it.

Wa lam tarqub qawli (ولم ترقب قولي): i.e., and you did not await my word concerning what you saw in that matter.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues with the dialogue that took place between Musa and his people after his return to them from the private conversation with his Lord. So His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Harun had already said to them before﴾, i.e., before Musa's return, while they were worshipping the calf: "O my people, indeed the calf is not your god, nor the god of Musa; it is only a trial. You have been tested by it, so that Allah may see your patience in worshipping it and your adherence to obeying His Messenger, and so that He may see otherwise, and recompense each according to what he deserves." And he said to them: ﴿And indeed your Lord is the Most Merciful﴾, whose mercy you have witnessed in all your life, so remember it, ﴿so follow me﴾ in worshipping Allah alone and abandoning the worship of others, ﴿and obey my command﴾, for I am Musa's successor, the Messenger, among you. But the misguided people answered with what Allah, exalted is He, related of them in His saying: ﴿They said, "We will not cease to remain devoted to it until Musa returns to us."﴾, i.e., we will not stop from its worship and from remaining around it.

When Musa heard what his people said, he turned to Harun, saying reproachfully, rebuking and blaming him: ﴿O Harun, what prevented you, when you saw them going astray, from following me?﴾, i.e., by worshipping the calf. ﴿Did you then disobey my command?﴾ Out of intense grief and the force of blame and rebuke, he seized his brother's head-hair with his right hand and took hold of his beard with his left, dragging him toward himself while rebuking and blaming him. Harun said: ﴿O son of my mother, do not seize my beard nor my head.﴾ Indeed, I have an excuse for not following you, which is that I feared, if I went to you with some of your people, who are the Muslims, and left behind others, who are the calf-worshippers, that you would say, ﴿"You have caused division among the Children of Israel,"﴾ and that would not please you. ﴿And you did not await my word﴾, i.e., you did not wait to hear my account of what I saw in that matter.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Disobedience to the Messenger leads to trial for the disobedient in his religion and his worldly life.

2- It is permissible to admonish and rebuke a beloved one when he falls short in what was entrusted to him.

3- It is permissible for one accused of negligence to offer an excuse, even if the accusation is true.

4- A mujtahid may err in his ijtihad, and he may also be correct.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 20, verses 99–104:

Explanation of the words:

*Kadhalika* (thus): that is, just as We have related to you this story, the story of Musa and Fir'awn and Musa and the Children of Isra'il, We relate to you some of the news of the messengers.

*Min ladunna dhikran* (from Us, a reminder): that is, a Qur'an, and it is the Noble Qur'an.

*Man a'rada 'anhu* (whoever turns away from it): that is, he does not believe in it, does not recite it, and does not act upon it.

*Wizran* (a burden): that is, a heavy load of sins.

*Yawma yunfakhu fi al-Sur* (the Day the Trumpet is blown): that is, the second blast, which is the blast of resurrection. *As-Sur* (the Trumpet) is the horn.

*Zurqan* (blue-eyed): that is, their eyes are blue and their faces are black, a sign that they are the people of the Blazing Fire (al-Jahim).

*Yatakhafatun baynahum* (they whisper among themselves): that is, they lower their voices and speak secretly among themselves, out of the intensity of the terror.

*Amthalahum tariqatan* (the most correct of them in way): that is, the most just of them in opinion on that matter. All of this is due to the greatness of the situation and the severity of the terror and fright.

The meaning of the verses:

After the conclusion of the account between Musa and Fir'awn, and between Musa and the Children of Isra'il, the Exalted said to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Thus do We relate to you﴾, that is, just as We have related to you the account of Musa and Fir'awn and the report of Musa and the Children of Isra'il, We relate to you ﴿some of the news of what has passed before﴾, that is, the events of the earlier nations, so that this be a sign of your prophethood and of Our revelation to you, and a lesson and a reminder for the believers. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We have certainly given you from Us a reminder﴾, that is, We have bestowed upon you, by Our grace, a reminder, which is the Mighty Qur'an, by which the servant remembers his Lord and is guided by it to the path of salvation and happiness. His saying ﴿Whoever turns away from it﴾, that is, from the Qur'an, not believing in it and not acting upon what is in it, ﴿indeed, he will bear on the Day of Resurrection a burden﴾, that is, a great sin, because he did not do righteous deeds, and all his deeds were evil due to his disbelief and lack of faith. ﴿Abiding therein﴾, that is, in that burden, in the Fire. His saying ﴿And evil for them will be that burden on the Day of Resurrection﴾, that is, that burden is wretched as a load on the Day of Resurrection, since its bearer is not saved from the punishment but is cast with it into Hell, where he abides forever. His saying ﴿The Day the Trumpet is blown, and We will gather the criminals﴾, that is, those who deny the true religion and who practise polytheism and sins, ﴿on that Day﴾, that is, the day the Trumpet is blown with the second blast, ﴿blue-eyed﴾, that is, with their eyes blue and their faces black. His saying: ﴿They will whisper among themselves﴾, that is, they will murmur to one another, each asking the other how long they remained in the world and in the graves, and one of them will say: ﴿You remained not but ten﴾, that is, you remained only ten nights.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿We know best what they say when their most just in opinion says: "You remained not but a day"﴾, that is, the most just of them in opinion. ﴿You remained not but a day﴾. This describing of the time as short is caused by the terror of the Resurrection and the greatness of the scenes of fear and punishment they witness therein.

Lessons from the verses:

1- The confirmation of the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ): the Exalted relates to him the news of what has passed before, after relating to him the news of Musa and Fir'awn with truth, and His giving him the Noble Qur'an.

2- The Qur'an is a reminder to those who remember, because of the proofs, evidences and demonstrations it carries.

3- The wretched state of the criminals on the Day of Resurrection, who turned away from the Noble Qur'an.

4- The greatness of the terrors of the Day of Resurrection, so that a person considers the duration of the life of this world, which is thousands of years, to be short in comparison.

The meaning of the verses:

After the conclusion of the account between Musa and Fir'awn, and between Musa and the Children of Isra'il, the Exalted said to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Thus do We relate to you﴾, that is, just as We have related to you the account of Musa and Fir'awn and the report of Musa and the Children of Isra'il, We relate to you ﴿some of the news of what has passed before﴾, that is, the events of the earlier nations, so that this be a sign of your prophethood and of Our revelation to you, and a lesson and a reminder for the believers.
