Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 20, verses 105–112:

Explanation of the words:

Yas'alunaka 'ani al-jibal (They ask you about the mountains): i.e., the polytheists ask about the mountains, how they will be on the Day of Resurrection.

Fa-qul yansifuha Rabbi nasfan (Say: My Lord will blow them away with a blowing): i.e., He will break them into pieces, then the winds will scatter them so they become scattered dust (habaan manthuran).

Qa'an safsafan (a level plain): i.e., even.

Iwajan wa la amtan (no curvature or unevenness): i.e., you will see in it neither depression nor elevation.

Al-da'i (the Caller): i.e., to the place of assembly (al-mahshar), calling them to it for presentation before the Lord, exalted is He.

Wa khasha'at al-aswat (and voices will be hushed): i.e., they will fall silent, so that nothing is heard except hams, which is the faint sound of footsteps.

Wa radiya lahu qawlan (and He is pleased with his word): by saying "There is no god but Allah" sincerely from his heart.

Wa la yuhituna bihi 'ilma (and they cannot encompass Him in knowledge): Allah, exalted is He, knows what is before people and what is behind them, while they cannot encompass Him in knowledge.

Wa 'anati al-wujuhu lil-hayyi al-qayyum (And faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting): i.e., they will be abased and submissive before the Lord, the Living who does not die.

Man hamala zulman (whoever carries wrongdoing): i.e., he comes on the Day of Resurrection carrying the burdens of wrongdoing, which is polytheism (shirk).

Zulman wa la hadman (fear no wrongdoing or diminishing): i.e., he does not fear that his evil deeds will be increased, nor that his good deeds will be diminished.

The meaning of the verses:

Allah, exalted is He, says to His Messenger: ﴿They ask you﴾, i.e., the polytheists among your people who deny the resurrection and recompense, ﴿about the mountains﴾, about their fate on the Day of Resurrection. So say to them: ﴿My Lord will blow them away with a blowing, then He will leave it a level plain, in which you will see no curvature or unevenness﴾. I.e., answer them that Allah, exalted is He, will break them into pieces and then blow them away so they become scattered dust, leaving their places as a level plain (qa'an safsafan), that is, a flat land in which you see neither curvature (iwajan) nor unevenness (amtan), i.e., neither depression nor elevation. And His saying: ﴿On that Day they will follow the Caller, with no crookedness to him, and voices will be hushed before the Most Merciful, so you will hear nothing but hams﴾, i.e., on the day the Resurrection occurs and they are raised, the Caller will call them: "Come to the place of assembly." They will not turn aside from his voice to the right or to the left, and this is the meaning of "with no crookedness to him." And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and voices will be hushed before the Most Merciful﴾, i.e., they will be abased and silent, ﴿so you will hear nothing but hams﴾, which is a faint sound like the sound of light-footed camels when they walk. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On that Day, intercession will not benefit, except from one whom the Most Merciful permits and whose word He approves﴾. I.e., Allah, exalted is He, informs that on the day they are gathered to the place of assembly for the judgment, no intercession of anyone will benefit anyone except one whom the Most Merciful has permitted to intercede, and whose word He approves, i.e., the one for whom intercession is made is among the people of monotheism, the people of "There is no god but Allah." And His saying: ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them, while they cannot encompass Him in knowledge﴾, i.e., He knows what is before the people of the assembly, that is, the judgment He will pass on them of Paradise or Hellfire, and what is behind them, that is, the deeds they left behind in the world, while they cannot encompass Him, mighty and majestic is He, in knowledge. Therefore the recompense will be just and merciful. And His saying: ﴿And faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting﴾, i.e., they will be abased and submissive, as a captive lowers his face, and the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting, is Allah, majestic is His majesty. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And he has failed who carries wrongdoing﴾, i.e., has lost, namely polytheism, and we seek refuge in Allah. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer﴾, the state being that he believes in Allah, His angels, His books, His messenger, the Last Day and the final resurrection, ﴿then he will not fear wrongdoing, by an increase in his evil deeds, nor diminishing, by a reduction of his good deeds﴾, and this is the justice of Allah, exalted is He, which is manifest in the station of reckoning and recompense.

Guidance from the verses:

Guidance from the verses:

1- Clarification of the ignorance of the polytheists in their question about the mountains.

2- Affirmation of the principle of the final resurrection.

3- There is no intercession for anyone other than the people of monotheism; a polytheist will not intercede, and no intercession will be made for a polytheist.

4- Clarification of the failure of the polytheists and the success of the monotheists on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 20, verses 105–112:

Explanation of the words:

Fa-qul yansifuha Rabbi nasfan (Say: My Lord will blow them away with a blowing): i.e., He will break them into pieces, then the winds will scatter them so they become scattered dust (habaan manthuran).

Qa'an safsafan (a level plain): i.e., even.

Iwajan wa la amtan (no curvature or unevenness): i.e., you will see in it neither depression nor elevation.

Al-da'i (the Caller): i.e., to the place of assembly (al-mahshar), calling them to it for presentation before the Lord, exalted is He.

Wa khasha'at al-aswat (and voices will be hushed): i.e., they will fall silent, so that nothing is heard except hams, which is the faint sound of footsteps.

Wa radiya lahu qawlan (and He is pleased with his word): by saying "There is no god but Allah" sincerely from his heart.

Wa la yuhituna bihi 'ilma (and they cannot encompass Him in knowledge): Allah, exalted is He, knows what is before people and what is behind them, while they cannot encompass Him in knowledge.

Wa 'anati al-wujuhu lil-hayyi al-qayyum (And faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting): i.e., they will be abased and submissive before the Lord, the Living who does not die.

Man hamala zulman (whoever carries wrongdoing): i.e., he comes on the Day of Resurrection carrying the burdens of wrongdoing, which is polytheism (shirk).

Zulman wa la hadman (fear no wrongdoing or diminishing): i.e., he does not fear that his evil deeds will be increased, nor that his good deeds will be diminished.

The meaning of the verses:

Allah, exalted is He, says to His Messenger: ﴿They ask you﴾, i.e., the polytheists among your people who deny the resurrection and recompense, ﴿about the mountains﴾, about their fate on the Day of Resurrection. And His saying: ﴿On that Day they will follow the Caller, with no crookedness to him, and voices will be hushed before the Most Merciful, so you will hear nothing but hams﴾, i.e., on the day the Resurrection occurs and they are raised, the Caller will call them: "Come to the place of assembly." I.e., Allah, exalted is He, informs that on the day they are gathered to the place of assembly for the judgment, no intercession of anyone will benefit anyone except one whom the Most Merciful has permitted to intercede, and whose word He approves, i.e., the one for whom intercession is made is among the people of monotheism, the people of "There is no god but Allah." Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 20, verses 113–115:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Wa-kadhalika anzalnahu﴾: That is, in the same manner as that revelation, We sent down the Qur'an in Arabic, that is, in the language of the Arabs, so that they might understand it.

﴿Wa-sarrafna fihi mina al-wa'id﴾: That is, of the various kinds of warning, and the varieties of punishment in this world and the Hereafter.

﴿Aw yuhdithu lahum dhikran﴾: That is, through the destruction of the earlier nations, so that they take heed, repent, and submit.

﴿Fa-ta'ala Allahu al-Malik al-Haqq﴾: That is, exalted above what the slanderers say and what the polytheists associate with Him.

﴿Wa-la ta'jal bil-Qur'an﴾: That is, do not hasten with its recitation.

﴿Min qabli an yuqda ilayka wahyuhu﴾: That is, before Jibril has finished reciting it to you.

﴿'Ahidna ila Adam﴾: That is, We commanded Adam and enjoined him not to eat from the tree.

﴿Fa-nasiya﴾: That is, he forgot Our covenant and abandoned it.

﴿Wa-lam najid lahu 'azma﴾: That is, resolve and patience in refraining from what We had forbidden him.

Meaning of the verses:

He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And thus have We sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an﴾, meaning: Just as We sent down those verses containing promise and warning, We sent down the Qur'an in the language of the Arabs so that they might understand it and be guided by it. ﴿And We have diversified in it of warning﴾, meaning: We have made clear in it various kinds of warning and repeated the varieties of punishment in this world and the Hereafter, so that perhaps your people, O Messenger, may guard against what caused the destruction of earlier nations, namely polytheism, denial, and sins. ﴿Or it causes them to remember﴾, meaning: it brings about in them a remembrance within themselves, so that they take heed, repent of polytheism and of denying the Messenger, obey their Lord, and thus prosper and find happiness. This is what the first verse [113] indicates.

As for the second verse, His saying ﴿So exalted is Allah, the True King﴾, Allah the Exalted informs of His highness above all His creation, His dominion over them, His disposal of them, and His subjugation of them. Therefore He is far above any partner or offspring, and above every deficiency that the slanderous liars attribute to Him.

His saying: ﴿And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation to you is completed﴾ teaches His Messenger the manner of receiving the Qur'an from Jibril, peace be upon him, guiding him that he should not hasten in reciting the verses, nor in dictating them to his companions, nor in judging by them, until Jibril has finished reciting them to him in full and the explanation of Allah's intended meaning in their revelation. He was asked to seek more knowledge, by His saying: ﴿And say: My Lord, increase me in knowledge﴾, and this implies that he is always in need of more; therefore one should not hasten but should be deliberate and unhurried. The scholars of his community are even more in need of this than he ﷺ, for hastiness in giving fatwas and in issuing rulings often leads their holder into error.

His saying: ﴿And We had already taken a covenant from Adam before, but he forgot, and We found in him no determination﴾ — Allah the Exalted, informing His Messenger and the believers, says: We had indeed enjoined Adam before these nations, whom We commanded and forbade, and most of them did not obey. We enjoined him not to obey his enemy Iblis and not to eat from the tree. He abandoned Our commandment, forgetting it, unconcerned with it, and obeyed his enemy and ate from the tree. ﴿And We found in him no determination﴾, rather he was weak before the enticement and adornment, so he did not keep the covenant nor persevere in obedience. How then would it be with other than Adam among all his descendants? Therefore you should not grieve or be saddened over your people's failure to believe in you and to respond to your call.

Guidance of the verses:

1. Clarification of the wisdom behind sending down the Qur'an in the Arabic tongue and the diversification of warning within it.

2. Affirmation of Allah's exaltedness, His dominion over His servants, His kingship over them, and His transcendence above offspring, partners, and every deficiency attributed to Him by the falsifiers.

3. Recommendation of deliberation and patience in reciting the Qur'an, interpreting it, and issuing judgments and fatwas from it.

4. Encouragement to seek knowledge and further learning, and to recognize one's own ignorance and need for knowledge.

5. Consolation through Adam's forgetfulness and the weakness of his heart before satanic enticement.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 20, verses 116–122:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And when We said to the angels﴾: i.e., remember Our saying, for admonition and lesson.

﴿Except Iblis; he refused﴾: i.e., he refused to prostrate out of arrogance within himself, since he was not of the angels; rather he was the father of the jinn. He was among the angels, worshipping Allah along with them.

﴿An enemy to you and to your wife﴾: i.e., Hawwa'. Meaning of "enemy": he does not wish you good, but wishes you evil.

﴿So that you become wretched﴾: i.e., through labour on the earth, for you would sow, reap, grind and bake until you have food to eat.

﴿That you will not hunger therein nor be naked, nor will you thirst therein or be exposed to the sun﴾: i.e., you will not be thirsty, nor will the painful heat of the midday sun strike you on the earth.

﴿The tree of eternity﴾: i.e., the tree whose eater lives forever.

﴿And a kingdom that does not decay﴾: i.e., that does not perish or come to an end, and this entails eternity.

﴿Then their private parts became apparent to them﴾: i.e., each of them saw the front and back of the other, and they were ashamed of that.

﴿And they began to cover themselves with the leaves of the garden﴾: i.e., they took and began to stick leaves of trees upon themselves as a covering for their private parts.

﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray﴾: i.e., by eating from the forbidden tree.

﴿Then his Lord chose him and turned to him in forgiveness and guided him﴾: i.e., He chose him for His guardianship, guided him to repentance, and he repented so that he might become a righteous servant.

Meaning of the verses:

When Allah, the Exalted, mentioned the weakness of Adam, peace be upon him, in that He had charged him not to obey Iblis lest he expel him and his wife from the Garden, and that Adam forgot the covenant and ate from the tree, it was fitting to mention the full story of Adam, to be an admonition to the righteous and a guidance to the believers. So Allah, the Exalted, said to His messenger Muhammad ﷺ: "And remember": ﴿And when We said to the angels: Prostrate yourselves before Adam﴾. Their prostration was worship of Allah, the Exalted, and a greeting to Adam for his nobility and knowledge. The angels complied with Allah's command ﴿so they prostrated﴾, all of them together, ﴿except Iblis; he refused﴾ to prostrate, because of the arrogance that entered him, and because he was not of the angels but of the jinn, although he used to worship Allah, the Exalted, with the angels in the heavens. This is what the first verse [116] indicates.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So We said: O Adam﴾, i.e., after Iblis became arrogant and refused to prostrate to Adam, We advised Adam and said to him: ﴿Indeed, this is an enemy to you and to your wife, so let him not expel you both from the Garden, so that you become wretched﴾, i.e., do not obey him, for his obedience would be the cause of your expulsion from the Garden, and once you are expelled you will be wretched. The address to Adam in His saying "so that you become wretched" is because the wretchedness meant here is labour, such as sowing, harvesting and other things necessary for living outside the Garden, and the husband is responsible for maintaining his wife, so it is he who becomes wretched on her behalf. And His saying to Adam: ﴿Indeed, it is granted to you that you will not hunger therein nor be naked﴾, i.e., in the Garden, ﴿and that you will not thirst therein nor be exposed to the sun﴾, i.e., you will not be thirsty, nor will you be exposed to the heat of the midday sun as it is on the earth. Although the address is to Adam, Hawwa' follows him by virtue of the husband's authority over his wife. And it is proper etiquette to address the man rather than his wife, since she follows him. And His saying: ﴿Then Satan whispered to him﴾, i.e., he called to him by way of whispering.

﴿O Adam, shall I guide you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?﴾ So Adam accepted this from him and responded to his whispering. Hawwa' ate first, then Adam ate, which is His saying: ﴿So they both ate from it﴾. Consequently, their private parts were revealed to them, the light that covered them having departed because of their disobedience to Allah, the Exalted. And His saying: ﴿And they began to cover themselves with the leaves of the garden﴾, i.e., they began to fasten the leaves of trees upon their private parts as a covering for them, because the sight of nakedness distresses a human being, and for this reason the private part is called "sawah" (that which causes distress). Thus Adam disobeyed his Lord by responding to the whisperings of his enemy and eating from the tree, and by that he went astray. Yet his Lord chose him, i.e., made him a prophet and brought him near as a friend, ﴿then He turned to him and guided him﴾, guiding him to act in obedience to Him, so that he would be among His chosen ones and righteous servants. And praise be to Allah, Lord of bounty and favour.

Lessons from the verses:

1- Establishing the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ by mentioning such stories, which are known only through divine revelation.

2- Establishing Iblis's enmity toward the children of Adam.

3- Explaining that there is no toil or fatigue in the Garden; these exist only on the earth.

4- Warning against the dangers of responding to Iblis's whisperings, for they cast their companion into ruin.

5- The weakness of women and their lack of resolve: she ate before Adam and thus made the disobedience easy for him.

6- The woman follows the man and has no right to be independent in any circumstance.

7- The prohibition of uncovering nakedness and the obligation to cover it.

8- Affirming the prophethood of Adam, Allah's acceptance of his repentance, and his guidance to acting in accordance with what Allah loves and avoiding what He dislikes.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So We said: O Adam﴾, i.e., after Iblis became arrogant and refused to prostrate to Adam, We advised Adam and said to him: ﴿Indeed, this is an enemy to you and to your wife, so let him not expel you both from the Garden, so that you become wretched﴾, i.e., do not obey him, for his obedience would be the cause of your expulsion from the Garden, and once you are expelled you will be wretched. The address to Adam in His saying "so that you become wretched" is because the wretchedness meant here is labour, such as sowing, harvesting and other things necessary for living outside the Garden, and the husband is responsible for maintaining his wife, so it is he who becomes wretched on her behalf. And His saying to Adam: ﴿Indeed, it is granted to you that you will not hunger therein nor be naked﴾, i.e., in the Garden, ﴿and that you will not thirst therein nor be exposed to the sun﴾, i.e., you will not be thirsty, nor will you be exposed to the heat of the midday sun as it is on the earth. Although the address is to Adam, Hawwa' follows him by virtue of the husband's authority over his wife. And it is proper etiquette to address the man rather than his wife, since she follows him. And His saying: ﴿Then Satan whispered to him﴾, i.e., he called to him by way of whispering.

﴿O Adam, shall I guide you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?﴾ So Adam accepted this from him and responded to his whispering. Hawwa' ate first, then Adam ate, which is His saying: ﴿So they both ate from it﴾. Consequently, their private parts were revealed to them, the light that covered them having departed because of their disobedience to Allah, the Exalted. And His saying: ﴿And they began to cover themselves with the leaves of the garden﴾, i.e., they began to fasten the leaves of trees upon their private parts as a covering for them, because the sight of nakedness distresses a human being, and for this reason the private part is called "sawah" (that which causes distress). Thus Adam disobeyed his Lord by responding to the whisperings of his enemy and eating from the tree, and by that he went astray. Yet his Lord chose him, i.e., made him a prophet and brought him near as a friend, ﴿then He turned to him and guided him﴾, guiding him to act in obedience to Him, so that he would be among His chosen ones and righteous servants. And praise be to Allah, Lord of bounty and favour.

Lessons from the verses:

1- Establishing the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ by mentioning such stories, which are known only through divine revelation.

2- Establishing Iblis's enmity toward the children of Adam.

3- Explaining that there is no toil or fatigue in the Garden; these exist only on the earth.

4- Warning against the dangers of responding to Iblis's whisperings, for they cast their companion into ruin.

5- The weakness of women and their lack of resolve: she ate before Adam and thus made the disobedience easy for him.

6- The woman follows the man and has no right to be independent in any circumstance.

7- The prohibition of uncovering nakedness and the obligation to cover it.

8- Affirming the prophethood of Adam, Allah's acceptance of his repentance, and his guidance to acting in accordance with what Allah loves and avoiding what He dislikes.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 20, verses 123–127:

Explanation of the words:

"He said: Go down from it, all of you" (qala ihbitu minha jami'an): That is, Adam and Hawwa' (Eve) from the Garden, and Iblis had already been made despairing and cast down before them.

"Some of you are enemies to others" (ba'dukum li ba'din 'aduw): That is, Adam, Hawwa' and their offspring are enemies to Iblis and his offspring, and Iblis and his offspring are enemies to Adam, Hawwa' and their offspring.

"Then, if guidance comes to you from Me" (fa-imma ya'tiyannakum minni huda): That is, if guidance comes to you from Me, which is the Book and the Messenger.

"Whoever follows My guidance" (faman ittaba'a huday): That is, what I sent with My Messenger, which is the Qur'an.

"he will not go astray" (fala yadillu): That is, in this world.

"nor will he be distressed" (wa-la yashqa): In the Hereafter.

"But whoever turns away from My remembrance" (waman a'rada 'an dhikri): That is, away from the Qur'an, so that he does not believe in it and does not act upon what is in it.

"a life of hardship" (ma'ishatan dankan): That is, a narrow life, in which his soul feels constricted, and he is not made happy by it, even if it is spacious.

"blind" (a'ma): That is, blind of sight, unable to see.

"though I was seeing" (wa-qad kuntu basiran): That is, possessing sight in this world and at the Resurrection.

"He will say: Thus" (qala kadhalika): That is, the matter is so: "Our signs came to you, and you forgot them, so just as you forgot them, you will be forgotten in Hell."

"And thus do We recompense the one who transgresses" (wa-kadhalika najzi man asraf): That is, and such is the recompense with which We repay the one who forgot Our signs: We recompense whoever transgresses in sins and does not stop at a limit, and does not believe in the signs of his Lord, glorified and exalted is He.

"more severe and more lasting" (ashaddu wa-abqa): That is, more severe than the punishment of this world and more enduring, never ceasing or ending.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with the story of Adam: when Adam and Hawwa' ate from the tree, their private parts became apparent to them, and their Lord rebuked them with His words in another verse: "Did I not forbid you from that tree and tell you that Satan is a clear enemy to you?" [al-A'raf: 22]. Adam received the word of repentance, said it together with his wife, and Allah turned to them in forgiveness. When all of that was complete, He said: "Go down from it" – that is, from the Garden – "all of you," since Iblis, the enemy, had already been made despairing and expelled from the Garden, so they all descended. As for His words "If guidance comes to you from Me" – that is, the clarification of My worship, carried by My Books and clarified by My Messengers – "whoever follows My guidance," believing in it and acting upon what is in it, "will not go astray" in his life, "nor will he be distressed" in his Hereafter. "But whoever turns away from My remembrance" – that is, does not believe in it and does not act upon what is in it – "then indeed for him" – that is, a recompense from Us – "is a life of hardship," narrow, in which his soul is constricted, so he does not feel contentment and happiness, even if his provision is abundant, just as his grave is constricted for him, and he will be wretched in it throughout the life of the barzakh (intermediate state). On the Day of Resurrection he will be gathered blind, having no proof and no sight with which to see. He will wonder at his condition and ask his Lord: "Why have You gathered me blind, when I was [in the world and at the resurrection] seeing?" His Lord, exalted, will answer him: "Thus" – that is, the matter is so: you were seeing and became blind, because "Our signs came to you," carried by Our Books and clarified by Our Messengers, "and you forgot them" – that is, you abandoned them and did not turn to them, turning away from them. So today you are left forgotten in Hell. As for His words, exalted, in the following verse [127]: "And thus do We recompense whoever transgresses" in Our disobedience, not stopping at a limit and not believing in the signs of his Lord, so We make for him a life of hardship in his worldly life and in the barzakh. "And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe" than the punishment of this world, "and more lasting" – that is, more enduring, never ceasing or ending.

1- Affirmation of Satan's enmity toward man.

2- Allah's promise to whoever believes in the Qur'an and acts upon what is in it: that he will not go astray in his life nor be distressed in his Hereafter.

3- Clarification of the recompense of whoever turns away from the Qur'an in this world and the Hereafter.

4- Condemnation of excess in sins and transgressions together with disbelief in the signs of Allah, and clarification of the recompense for that.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 20, verses 128–132:

Explanation of the words:

"Afalam yahdi lahum" (Has it not become clear to them?): i.e., has it not been made clear to them?

"Min al-qurun" (from the generations): i.e., from the peoples of the past generations.

"La-ayatin li-ulil-nuha" (are signs for people of sound intellect): i.e., for people of sound reason, since al-nuha (intellect) is reason.

"Wa-lawla kalimatun sabaqat" (And had it not been for a word that had already gone forth): i.e., the postponement of the punishment from them.

"La-kana lizaman" (the punishment would have been inevitable): i.e., the punishment would have been binding and would in no way have been delayed for them.

"Ma yaqulun" (what they say): i.e., of the words of disbelief and of their demands for signs.

"Wa-min anha'i al-layl" (and during the hours of the night): i.e., the hours of the night, the singular of which is inyun or inwun.

"La'allaka tarda" (so that you may be pleased): i.e., in hope that you will be rewarded with the good reward with which you are pleased.

"Ila ma mtana bihi azwajan minhum" (to what We have given to pairs of them): i.e., to men among them who are disbelievers.

Perhaps by this you will be pleased with the reward of Allah the Exalted for you.

His saying: ﴿And do not extend your eyes﴾, i.e., do not look with longing eyes ﴿toward what We have given pairs of them to enjoy﴾, i.e., varieties in their beliefs, morals, and conduct, ﴿the splendour of the life of this world﴾, i.e., of the adornment of the life of this world, ﴿that We may test them thereby﴾, i.e., that We may try them by what We have given them of the adornment of the life of this world. His saying: ﴿But the provision of your Lord﴾, i.e., what you have from God of reward and recompense, ﴿is better and more lasting﴾, better in its kind and more lasting in its duration. Preferring the lasting over the transient is the aim of people of intellect.

His saying: ﴿And enjoin prayer upon your family and be steadfast in it﴾, i.e., your wives, daughters, and believing followers, to pray. In it lie refuge and healing from the pains of need and poverty. Be steadfast in it, and compel yourself to be patient in establishing it. His saying: ﴿We do not ask you for provision﴾, i.e., We do not burden you with wealth to give Us, but We ask you to perform prayer, so perform it in its most complete form. ﴿We provide for you﴾, i.e., your provision is upon Us, ﴿and the good end is for taqwa﴾, i.e., the praiseworthy outcome in this world and the Hereafter belongs to the people of taqwa among Our servants, who fear Us, fulfil what We have made obligatory upon them, and avoid what We have forbidden them, out of awe of Us and desire for what is with Us. For these there are the best outcomes they reach: victory in this world and happiness in the Hereafter.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Establishing the principle that the intelligent person takes warning from others.

2- Explaining the virtue of intellect, the nobility of its possessor, and his benefit from it.

3- The obligation of patience in calling to God, and seeking help in that through prayer.

4- Explaining the times of the five prayers, and attaining the soul's contentment through their reward.

5- The obligation of not attaching the soul to the wealth and goods of the disbelievers, because they are being tested by them.

6- The obligation of contentment with what God has apportioned to the servant as provision, in anticipation of the everlasting, enduring provision of the Hereafter.

7- The obligation of enjoining prayer upon family, children, and Muslims, and being patient in that.

8- The excellence of taqwa and the honour of its people, and their success in the good end in this world and the Hereafter.

9- Establishing prayer among the members of a Muslim family, through which Allah facilitates the means of provision and grants them abundance.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 20, verses 133–135:

Explanation of the words:

"Lawla" (لولا): that is, "halla" (هلّا, "why not"). It is a particle of urging and exhortation toward the occurrence of what is mentioned after it.

"Bi-ayatin min rabbihi" (بآية من ربه): that is, a miracle that demonstrates his truthfulness in his prophethood and messengership.

"Bayyinatu ma fi al-suhuf al-ula" (بينة ما في الصحف الأولى): that is, what the Great Qur'an contains of the reports of past nations and their destruction for denying their messengers.

"Min qablihi" (من قبله): before Our sending Our messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) and Our sending down Our Book, the Qur'an.

"Min qabli an nadhilla wa nukhza" (من قبل أن نذل ونخزى): that is, before humiliation and disgrace befall us on the Day of Resurrection in Hell.

"Mutarabbis" (متربص): that is, awaiting what the matter will lead to.

"Fa-sa-ta'lamun" (فستعلمون): that is, on the Day of Resurrection.

"As-sirat as-sawi" (الصراط السوي): that is, the correct religion, which is Islam.

"Wa man ihtada" (ومن اهتدى): that is, of those who went astray, "we or you."

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues with the polytheists, seeking their guidance. Allah the Exalted says, reporting about those polytheists whom Allah granted enjoyment of the splendour of the worldly life, that they persisted in polytheism and denial: ﴿And they say: "Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?"﴾ That is: why does Muhammad not bring us a miracle like those that Salih, Moses and Jesus son of Mary brought, which demonstrates his truthfulness in his prophethood and messengership to us? Allah the Exalted said, refuting their false statement: ﴿Has there not come to them the clear proof of what is in the former scriptures?﴾ Do they demand signs while the clear proof of what is in the former scriptures has come to them through the Noble Qur'an? They have known what befell the nations that demanded signs, and when the signs came to them they denied them, so Allah destroyed them for their denial. So what assurance is there that these polytheists who demand signs will believe if they come? They would not believe in them, and would be destroyed as the deniers before them were destroyed.

As for His saying in the second verse [134]: ﴿And had We destroyed them with a punishment before it﴾ — that is, before Our sending Muhammad and sending the Book down upon him — they would have said to the Lord, Exalted is He, when they stood before Him: ﴿Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so that we might follow Your signs?﴾ in what You call us to of monotheism, faith and righteous deeds, and that is before we were humiliated in this humiliation and disgraced in this disgrace in the fire of Hell. If this is what they would say without doubt, then why do they not believe and follow the signs of Allah, acting upon what came in them of guidance before the punishment descends upon them? In the last verse, after this guidance that He directed them to, Allah the Exalted said to His Messenger: ﴿Say: "Each is waiting"﴾ — that is, each of us is waiting, that is, awaiting what the matter will lead to — ﴿so wait﴾. ﴿Soon you will know﴾ at the end of the matter, when you are made to stand in the plains of Resurrection, ﴿who﴾ are ﴿the companions of the even path﴾ that has no crookedness, which is Islam, the true religion, ﴿and who is guided﴾ to the path of salvation and happiness, ﴿from among those who have gone astray.﴾ Such a one has lost and perished.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Demanding signs is a practice followed by nations and peoples when they turn away from the truth and disown reason and its guidance.

2- Humiliation and disgrace befall the people of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection because of what they neglected of faith and righteous deeds.

3- In the verse there is an allusion to the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (رضي الله عنه): "Three will argue before Allah on the Day of Resurrection: the one who died in the interval (al-fatra), the one overcome in his intellect, and the young child. The one overcome in his intellect will say: 'You did not give me intellect by which I could benefit.' The one who died in the interval will say: 'No messenger or prophet came to me; if a messenger or prophet had come to me, I would have been the most obedient of Your creation to You.' And he (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger?﴾ And the young child will say: 'I was a child and did not understand.'

He said: Then a fire will be raised for them, and it will be said to them: 'Enter it.' He said: Whoever was known in Allah's knowledge to be fortunate will enter it, and whoever was known in Allah's knowledge to be wretched will hold back from it. Then He will say: 'You disobeyed Me, so how much more would you have disobeyed My messengers had they come to you.'"
